bug_description.original: A vulnerability exists in the loop restoration multi-threading code where, when luma loop restoration is disabled, the initialization of cur_sb_col in lr_sync does not occur correctly.
bug_description.normalized: The staged 219-byte AV1 witness reaches `decode_restoration_mode()`, where frame-header bits set plane 0 to `RESTORE_NONE` while leaving at least one chroma plane enabled and deriving the active chroma `restoration_unit_size`. `av1_alloc_restoration_struct()` turns those parsed sizes into per-plane `vert_units_per_tile`, and `av1_loop_restoration_filter_frame_init()` copies each active plane's `rsi` pointer and whole-frame `tile_rect` into `lr_ctxt->ctxt[plane]` while skipping disabled planes. In the vulnerable threaded path, `foreach_rest_unit_in_planes_mt()` still iterates every plane, sizes `num_rows_lr` from `ctxt[plane].tile_rect`, and hardcodes the sequence superblock size instead of using each active plane's parsed `restoration_unit_size`. `loop_restoration_alloc()` therefore allocates `cur_sb_col` and `job_queue` for only `num_rows_lr * num_planes` row slots, but `enqueue_lr_jobs()` later skips inactive planes and enqueues one job per actual restoration row for each active plane using `ctxt[plane].rsi->restoration_unit_size` and `vert_units_per_tile`. When the total queued active-plane rows exceeds that allocation, the first overflowing store is `lr_job_queue[lr_job_counter[i & 1]].lr_unit_row = i;` in `av1/common/thread_common.c:599`, matching the saved ASan report. The fix adds the missing `RESTORE_NONE` skip and uses `cm->rst_info[plane].restoration_unit_size` when computing `num_rows_lr`.

RESTORE_SWITCHABLE : RESTORE_NONE; } if (rsi->frame_restoration_type != RESTORE_NONE) { all_none = 0; chroma_none &= p == 0; }
source.description: The frame-header parser first materializes the attacker-controlled per-plane restoration-mode state. On the crashing path, plane 0 becomes `RESTORE_NONE` while at least one chroma plane remains enabled, so loop restoration stays on even though luma restoration is disabled.
source.value_from: The staged 219-byte `poc` is decoded as an AV1 frame, and `decode_restoration_mode()` consumes its header bits through `aom_rb_read_bit(rb)` at `decodeframe.c:1679-1684` to populate `cm->rst_info[*].frame_restoration_type` plus the `all_none`/`chroma_none` state that controls the vulnerable threaded path.

root_cause.code: for (int plane = 0; plane < num_planes; plane++) { const AV1PixelRect tile_rect = ctxt[plane].tile_rect; const int max_tile_h = tile_rect.bottom - tile_rect.top; const int unit_size = cm->seq_params.sb_size == BLOCK_128X128 ? 128 : 64; num_rows_lr = AOMMAX(num_rows_lr, av1_lr_count_units_in_tile(unit_size, max_tile_h)); }
root_cause.description: The vulnerable sizing loop still iterates every plane after `av1_loop_restoration_filter_frame_init()` skipped disabled ones, reads `ctxt[plane].tile_rect`, and hardcodes the sequence superblock size instead of each active plane's parsed `restoration_unit_size`. That can make `num_rows_lr` smaller than the actual active-plane row count later used by `enqueue_lr_jobs()`, under-sizing both `cur_sb_col` and `job_queue`. The patch fixes both obligations here.

sink.description: Source-level sink. Once `lr_job_counter[i & 1]` advances past the `num_rows_lr * num_planes` allocation from `loop_restoration_alloc()`, this 4-byte store writes into the heap redzone; AddressSanitizer reports the same write at `thread_common.c:599:55`.

tainted_value_origin.description: The header parser derives the shared chroma `restoration_unit_size` from attacker-controlled bits and copies it to plane 2. The active chroma plane contexts later use that parsed size to determine the actual restoration row count enqueued into `job_queue`.

parser_admitted.description: The uncompressed-frame-header parser has reached the restoration syntax branch, so `decode_restoration_mode(cm, rb)` now consumes attacker-controlled loop-restoration mode and unit-size bits from the staged AV1 frame.

coarse_trace.summary: The frame-header parser reads per-plane restoration-mode bits, disables luma restoration, keeps chroma restoration enabled, and derives the chroma restoration-unit size from attacker-controlled header bits.
Restoration metadata is allocated from the parsed per-plane unit sizes, storing each plane's actual `vert_units_per_tile`.
Because at least one plane still has loop restoration enabled and the crashing run used multiple workers, the decoder enters the threaded loop-restoration path.
Threaded loop-restoration setup aliases each active plane's `rsi` and whole-frame `tile_rect` into `lr_ctxt->ctxt[plane]`, while disabled planes are skipped.
The vulnerable sizing loop still iterates every plane and uses a fixed 64/128 superblock size, so `num_rows_lr` can underestimate the active-plane restoration row count.
Job enqueueing skips inactive planes and uses each active plane's real restoration geometry, so the queued jobs can exceed the undersized `job_queue` allocation and overflow it.

RESTORE_SWITCHABLE : RESTORE_NONE; } if (rsi->frame_restoration_type != RESTORE_NONE) { all_none = 0; chroma_none &= p == 0; }
fine_trace.note: The decoder consumes attacker-controlled restoration-mode bits from the frame header. On the crashing path, plane 0 is parsed as `RESTORE_NONE` while at least one chroma iteration clears `all_none` and `chroma_none`, so frame restoration remains enabled even though luma restoration is off.

fine_trace.code: if (!all_none) { const int sb_size = cm->seq_params.sb_size == BLOCK_128X128 ? 128 : 64; for (int p = 0; p < num_planes; ++p) cm->rst_info[p].restoration_unit_size = sb_size; if (sb_size == 64) { rsi->restoration_unit_size <<= aom_rb_read_bit(rb); } if (rsi->restoration_unit_size > 64) { rsi->restoration_unit_size <<= aom_rb_read_bit(rb); } }
fine_trace.note: Because step 1 left `all_none = 0`, the parser seeds every plane's `restoration_unit_size` from the sequence superblock size and then consumes one or two more header bits to choose plane 0's base restoration-unit size.

fine_trace.code: if (num_planes > 1) { int s = AOMMIN(cm->seq_params.subsampling_x, cm->seq_params.subsampling_y); if (s && !chroma_none) { cm->rst_info[1].restoration_unit_size = cm->rst_info[0].restoration_unit_size >> (aom_rb_read_bit(rb) * s); } else { cm->rst_info[1].restoration_unit_size = cm->rst_info[0].restoration_unit_size; } cm->rst_info[2].restoration_unit_size = cm->rst_info[1].restoration_unit_size; }
fine_trace.note: With chroma present on the crashing path, the parser derives the shared chroma restoration-unit size from plane 0's base size and copies it to plane 2. Any enabled chroma plane later uses this parsed size to determine its actual restoration row count.

fine_trace.note: Restoration metadata records each plane's actual vertical restoration-row count from that plane's parsed `restoration_unit_size`. The active chroma plane's `vert_units_per_tile` later drives how many jobs are enqueued.

fine_trace.code: const int do_loop_restoration = cm->rst_info[0].frame_restoration_type != RESTORE_NONE || cm->rst_info[1].frame_restoration_type != RESTORE_NONE || cm->rst_info[2].frame_restoration_type != RESTORE_NONE; ... if (do_loop_restoration) { if (pbi->num_workers > 1) { av1_loop_restoration_filter_frame_mt(...); } }
fine_trace.note: The parsed restoration-mode state makes `do_loop_restoration` true, and the saved ASan stack shows the multi-worker call reached `av1_loop_restoration_filter_frame_mt()`. The staged artifacts do not distinguish whether execution used the call site at `decodeframe.c:5230-5234` or the optimized call site at `5245-5249`, but both require the same restoration predicate and `pbi->num_workers > 1`.

fine_trace.note: Threaded restoration setup only populates `lr_ctxt->ctxt[plane]` for active planes. Disabled planes are skipped, while each active plane receives an alias to its `rsi` plus the whole-frame geometry that the later worker code reads through `ctxt[plane]`.

fine_trace.code: for (int plane = 0; plane < num_planes; plane++) { const AV1PixelRect tile_rect = ctxt[plane].tile_rect; const int max_tile_h = tile_rect.bottom - tile_rect.top; const int unit_size = cm->seq_params.sb_size == BLOCK_128X128 ? 128 : 64; num_rows_lr = AOMMAX(num_rows_lr, av1_lr_count_units_in_tile(unit_size, max_tile_h)); }

The sizing loop still iterates every plane even when step 6 skipped disabled ones, and it hardcodes the sequence superblock size instead of each active plane's parsed `restoration_unit_size`. With luma disabled and chroma still active, the resulting `num_rows_lr` can be smaller than the actual active-plane restoration row count later consumed by `enqueue_lr_jobs()`.

fine_trace.code: for (int j = 0; j < num_planes; j++) { CHECK_MEM_ERROR(cm, lr_sync->cur_sb_col[j], aom_malloc(sizeof(*(lr_sync->cur_sb_col[j])) * num_rows_lr)); } CHECK_MEM_ERROR(cm, lr_sync->job_queue, aom_malloc(sizeof(*(lr_sync->job_queue)) * num_rows_lr * num_planes));
fine_trace.note: The underestimated `num_rows_lr` from step 7 sizes both synchronization state and the job queue. That matches the issue description's `cur_sb_col` under-initialization, and the saved ASan trace shows the first concrete out-of-bounds access on the same allocation block for `job_queue`.

fine_trace.code: if (cm->rst_info[plane].frame_restoration_type == RESTORE_NONE) continue; num_even_lr_jobs += ((ctxt[plane].rsi->vert_units_per_tile + 1) >> 1); ... AV1PixelRect tile_rect = ctxt[plane].tile_rect; const int unit_size = ctxt[plane].rsi->restoration_unit_size; ... while (y0 < tile_h) { ... lr_job_counter[i & 1]++; y0 += h; ++i; }
fine_trace.note: Job enqueueing processes only active planes. It seeds the odd/even split from each active plane's actual `vert_units_per_tile`, then walks that plane's real `tile_rect` with its real `restoration_unit_size`, advancing `lr_job_counter` once per actual restoration row. The only in-loop assertion checks the even/odd partition, not `job_queue` bounds.

Once `lr_job_counter[i & 1]` reaches the first index beyond the step-8 `num_rows_lr * num_planes` allocation, this 4-byte store writes into the heap redzone. The saved AddressSanitizer report identifies the same write at `thread_common.c:599:55`.

format.name: av1 bitstream
format.contract: An AV1 frame whose restoration header reaches `decode_restoration_mode()`, sets plane 0 to `RESTORE_NONE`, leaves at least one chroma plane restoration-enabled, and gives the active chroma plane(s) a parsed `restoration_unit_size`/`vert_units_per_tile` that makes `enqueue_lr_jobs()` enqueue more actual restoration rows than the `num_rows_lr * num_planes` entries allocated by `foreach_rest_unit_in_planes_mt()` when it sizes rows from the fixed `cm->seq_params.sb_size` estimate on the threaded path (`pbi->num_workers > 1`).
